battle.name: 齊國繼承人戰爭
battle.theater: 齊國都城臨淄及宋魯地界
battle.brief: 公元前643年冬，齊桓公在位四十三年後去世，齊國分立諸公子，太子昭出奔宋國；前642年夏，宋襄公率諸侯之師伐齊，齊人不能戰而請和，聯軍進逼臨淄，齊國乃殺公子無虧，迎太子昭回國即位，是為齊威公。卡面的亞述長矛早本役二百五十七年，當時亞述巴尼拔仍在位，而東方齊國靠青銅戈矛與兵車守成。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 齊國繼承人戰爭是公元前643年至前642年，發生在春秋開端的齊國與宋國聯軍之間的一場因王位繼承而起的干涉戰爭。交戰的一方是姜姓呂氏的齊國：前643年冬，齊桓公在位四十三年後於臨淄宮中去世，臨終並未留下得到朝野認可的安排，齊國隨即分立諸位公子，太子昭出奔宋國，公子無虧被安置在莒邑，餘下公子各自結黨，國中公族分成數派，禁軍與宮禁之權落在內豎易牙、豎貂與公子開方一系手上，齊國的君位、兵權與賦稅一時無人統一支配。另一方是宋國及其率領的諸侯聯軍：宋襄公自前651年即以國君身分在位，此時正以承繼齊桓公霸業自任，宋國力小而諸侯信用尚存，於是集合魯、陳、蔡、許等與宋同會於齊的諸國軍隊，以送還合法繼承人為名出兵；史籍只稱「諸侯之師」，未列明全部國家。另外還有並未直接作戰但影響局面的第三方：魯國隱公在位而無力仲裁，宋國之內宋公馮死後兄弟爭位的餘波未平，衛、鄭等國在齊桓公九合諸侯的會盟體系中居於附庸地位，目睹齊國虛實而各自保留，楚國則正沿長江流域擴張，尚無介入東方的打算。整場衝突的規模在春秋初期屬罕見：它不是兩國之間的疆土爭奪，而是一次由外國聯軍以武力作後盾、替一個大國挑選君主的政治戰。
countriesEn: The War of Qi's Succession was an intervention fought between the state of Qi and a coalition led by Song in the opening years of the Spring and Autumn period, between 643 and 642 BC, and it grew out of a dispute over the succession to the throne. One side was Qi, of the Jiang surname and the Lü clan: in the winter of 643 BC, after forty-three years on the throne, Duke Huan of Qi died in his palace at Linzi, and he left behind no arrangement that the court at large would accept. The Qi people thereupon set up several of the dukes' sons in turn, the crown prince Zhao fled to Song, Prince Wufu was installed at the town of Ju, and the remaining princes formed their own factions, while the palace guard and the authority of the inner court fell to the eunuch favourites Yi Ya, Shu Diao and Prince Kaifang. For a time the throne, the armed force and the revenues of Qi were no longer under any single direction. The other side was Song and the coalition of lords it led: Duke Xiang of Song had reigned since 651 BC and now set himself up as the successor to Duke Huan's hegemony. Song was a small state, but its credit among the lords was still good, so it gathered the troops of Lu, Chen, Cai, Xu and the other states that met in Qi's assemblies — the chronicles say only 'the army of the lords' and do not name them all — and marched under the banner of restoring the rightful heir. Others took no direct part but shaped the outcome: Duke Yin of Lu remained silent and would not arbitrate; within Song the disorders left over from the rivalry that followed the death of Duke Feng had not yet settled; Wei and Zheng, still subordinate within the covenant built by Duke Huan's assemblies, watched Qi's weakness and held their cards close; and Chu was busy expanding along the Yangtze with no intention of reaching so far east. The scale of the affair was remarkable for the early Spring and Autumn: it was not a dispute over territory between two states, but a political war in which a foreign coalition used armed force as the prop behind the choice of a ruler for a great state.
people: 齊國這邊的關鍵人物大半集中在一個人的身後。齊桓公姬姓呂氏，名小白，前685年自莒國返國即位，在位四十三年，是春秋第一位以「尊王攘夷」號令諸侯的霸主；他用人唯才是舉，由鮑叔牙讓出相位而引進管仲，創下「九合諸侯，一匡天下」的會盟紀錄，齊國在他手中由東方諸國變成會盟的會主。然而自前645年管仲病故起，齊桓公晚年聽任易牙、豎貂與公子開方參預國政，長子太子昭的儲位屢遭削弱，臨終前的安排因而漏洞百出，史家記載他死後屍身久停方得入殮。齊國大夫歸生當年曾就寵信易牙、豎貂一事進諫，指出以寵幸之臣執掌內政將開亂源；此後公族高氏、國氏與陳氏（田氏之祖）各擁一端，爭的就是誰能在新君之下保住自己的位置。太子昭年幼無權，奔宋之後只能靠外國的兵；被立於莒邑的公子無虧自有武裝支持，成為齊國內部被推翻的一方；後來被迎回臨淄登基的，就是齊威公，他即位後數年間兩度用兵於魯，把魯國重新壓回會盟的秩序裡。聯軍一方的主角是宋襄公，他名目夷，父宋公馮死後於前651年即位，此時正處在齊國霸權真空與自身聲望的關鍵點上；他以諸侯之師的名義出動，在齊人請和時堅持送還太子昭，事後卻在泓之戰中把宋國的虛實暴露無遺，前638年重傷、前637年去世。魯國隱公在整場危機裡保持沉默，既不助宋也不助齊，只與齊國維持會盟關係，於是齊國得以在幾年之後重新站穩東方的位置。
peopleEn: Most of the decisive figures on Qi's side are gathered in the shadow of a single man. Duke Huan of Qi, of the Jiang surname and the Lü clan, was named Xiaobai; he returned from the state of Ju and took the throne in 685 BC, and his forty-three years of rule made him the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn to give orders to the lords in the name of 'honouring the king and repelling the barbarians'. He appointed men on their merits alone, taking the post of minister from Bao Shuya, who yielded it to Guan Zhong, and he built up the record of assemblies at which 'nine times he brought the lords together and set the realm in order'. Yet from the death of Guan Zhong in 645 BC onward, Duke Huan allowed the eunuch favourites Yi Ya, Shu Diao and Prince Kaifang to take part in government; the position of his eldest son, the crown prince Zhao, was repeatedly weakened, and the arrangement made at the end of his life was full of holes — the historians record that his body lay unburied for a long while before it could be coffined. The Qi minister Gui Sheng had already remonstrated over the favour shown to Yi Ya and Shu Diao, warning that letting favourites of this kind handle the interior would open the way to disorder; after that, the great clans of the state — the Guo, the Gao and the Chen, the Chen being the ancestor of the later Tian clan — each took a side, and what they fought over was who could keep their position under the new ruler. The crown prince Zhao was young and had no power of his own; once he had fled to Song, he could depend on nothing but the troops of a foreign state. Prince Wufu, who had been set up at Ju, had armed support of his own and became the man who was overturned inside Qi. The one later welcomed back to Linzi and raised to the throne was Duke Wei of Qi, and within a few years of his accession he twice took the field against Lu and pushed that state back into the order of the assemblies. The leading figure of the coalition was Duke Xiang of Song, named Mu Yi, who had taken the throne in 651 BC after the death of his father Duke Feng and who now stood at the decisive moment of his career, with a vacuum in Qi's hegemony and his own reputation still to be made. He moved out under the banner of the army of the lords and, when Qi asked for terms, insisted on the return of the crown prince Zhao; in the end, however, the battle of Hong stripped his state of its strength in front of the other lords, and he was wounded in 638 BC and dead in 637 BC. Duke Yin of Lu said nothing throughout the crisis, helping neither Song nor Qi and merely keeping up the covenant with Qi, and so Qi was allowed to re-establish itself in the east a few years later.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛是全場最刺眼的一件不相稱之物：它成器於公元前九百年，比本役早了二百五十七年，來自新亞述帝國的軍械序列，短柄、長刃、配鐵製矛鏃。前643年的亞述帝國仍在亞述巴尼拔統治之下，亞述浮雕所見的步兵長矛正是這種柄短而刃長、鏃作柳葉形、下端套筒固定的形制，亞述人正是靠長矛連同弓與鐵器，一城一城地壓平了兩河流域與埃蘭，所以這件兵器在同期並非過時之物，只是它不在東方。前643年的齊國及諸侯，長兵器的主力是青銅戈與矛：齊國的步兵是典型的戈兵，一手持戈、一手持盾，戈以銅鑄的鉤啄裝在柲上，主要用於鉤啄與近身擊刺；矛則是木柄加青銅矛頭，柄長約兩米，構成春秋兵陣中最基本的刺擊兵器。吳越一系在同一時期把矛與戈合鑄成一件，戈矛兼具刺與鉤，是當時最先進的長兵，考古出土的吳越戈矛器形修長，柲上常見細密幾何紋與鳥獸紋。齊國賦制把兵員折算為「戈」來計算，一繳出若干戈即出若干甲士，可見戈兵在齊國是制式裝備。防具方面，甲士多穿皮甲（革甲）與魚鱗式的青銅甲片，盾以木胎蒙皮為主；弓箭是各國都有的近身與中距武器；兵車仍是各國軍隊的骨架，一乘三人，御者居中、持戈者在右、徒在左，齊國的戰車與步兵配合是桓公霸業的底子。攻城手段仍以穴地逼近、塞門拒守、築土填堑與矢弩壓制為主，能登城的雲梯與能拋石的飛車要到戰國時代的《墨子》才留下詳細記載，而楚國的巢車、夷車這類觀察敵陣的高車，前597年鄢陵之戰才見於《左傳》。全場沒有火藥兵器，沒有重型衝撞車，也沒有騎兵大規模投入，這些都要再等數百年。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is the most striking anachronism in the whole affair: it was made in about 900 BC, some two hundred and fifty-seven years before this campaign, and it belongs to the arsenal series of the Neo-Assyrian state — a short shaft, a long blade and an iron head. In 643 BC the Assyrian empire was still under Ashurbanipal, and the spears carried by the infantry in the Assyrian reliefs are exactly of this build: a short grip, a long blade, a leaf-shaped head fitted into a socket at the bottom. It was with the spear, together with the bow and with iron, that the Assyrians pressed the cities of Mesopotamia and Elam down one after another, so the weapon was not obsolete in its own day; it was simply not in the east. In Qi's time and among the other lords, the backbone of the long weapon was the bronze ge and the mao: Qi's foot were typically ge-armed, carrying a ge in one hand and a shield in the other, the ge being a bronze hook-and-beak blade mounted on a shaft and used mainly for hooking and for close work; the mao was a wooden shaft with a bronze head, about two metres long, and it formed the most basic thrusting arm of the Spring and Autumn battle line. In the same period the Wu and Yue peoples cast the ge and the mao together into a single piece, the ge-mao combining a point and a hook, and this was the most advanced long weapon of the day; the ge-mao pieces excavated from Wu and Yue tombs are slender, their shafts often carrying fine geometric patterns and bird-and-beast motifs. The fiscal system of Qi reckoned the manning of its army in ge, a levy of so many ge producing so many armoured men, which shows that the ge-armed soldier was the standard equipment of the state. For protection, the armoured men wore hide coats and scale-like plates of bronze, and shields were wood covered with hide; the bow and arrow were the close and mid-range weapons common to every state; and the war chariot remained the skeleton of every army, carrying three men, the driver in the middle, the ge-armed soldier on the right and the attendant on the left, and Qi's combination of chariot and foot was the base on which the hegemony of Duke Huan was built. Siege methods still ran on tunnelling up to the wall, barricading the gates, filling the ditch with earth and pressure from arrows and crossbows; ladders for scaling a wall and engines for throwing stones are described in detail only in the Mozi of the Warring States period, and the tall observation cars of Chu, the nest-carts and the barrow-carts, appear in the Zuo Zhuan only at the battle of Yanling in 597 BC. There were no gunpowder weapons in this campaign, no heavy battering rams, and no large-scale use of cavalry; all of these had to wait for centuries to come.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術重點不在兩軍對撞，而在聯軍如何利用齊國的內裂。齊國的處境是典型的「中央失能」：國君一死，禁軍歸於內豎與公族各派，數股武裝各自據守城邑與封地，兵符、鼓與輜重分散，命令出不了臨淄；所以《左傳》記宋公以諸侯伐齊時說齊人「弗能戰」，不是沒有兵，而是沒有能統一全軍的指揮。宋國的做法是把會盟體系直接轉成軍事聯盟：宋襄公以本國兵為骨幹，諸侯各出車徒，聯軍自商丘向西北推進，經陶、曹一線再折向泰山南北通道，最後抵達齊都臨淄，全程約三百五十公里，按古代行軍每日三十至五十公里的常態速度，十日上下即可推進到城下，關鍵不在速度而在聯軍的糧秣與紀律能否維持。包圍臨淄之後，宋襄公沒有選擇強攻城郭——春秋的城牆與攻具尚不足以讓聯軍在短期內強行破城；他以兵威為談判的後盾，要求齊國必須按名分安置已出奔的太子昭。齊國的應對是先求和、再內整，終於自行清除了最刺眼的反對者：聯軍逼近，國人自居的公族在城內火併，殺掉公子無虧，迎太子昭回國，齊國以內部妥協換取聯軍退去。整個過程顯示春秋初期「以兵促立」的邏輯：聯軍並不打算兼併齊國，它的目標是讓一個得到諸侯承認的齊君回位，齊桓公時代建立的會盟秩序因此得以延續。相反，宋國的這一課代價慘痛：它用聯軍的旗號換來了政治上的即位之功，卻沒有在會戰中建立威勢，一年後的泓之戰便以宋軍大敗、宋襄公重傷收場。齊國這邊也有教訓：內亂一旦引來外國兵車，無論哪一黨勝出，都要付出讓外國勢力介入本國內政的代價。整場衝突沒有大規模攻城戰與會戰的記載，但它確定了春秋前期的兩個規則：一是霸權交接可以通過聯盟與內政程序完成，未必要靠城下的廢殺；二是齊國的公族必須找到一個新共識，否則類似的危機還會再來。
tacticsEn: The tactical centre of this war lay not in any clash of armies but in the way the coalition exploited the rift inside Qi. Qi's condition was the classic one of failed central command: once the ruler was dead, the palace guard passed to the eunuch party and to the separate clans, several armed groups held their own towns and fiefs, the tally sticks, the drums and the baggage were dispersed, and orders could not get out of Linzi. That is why the Zuo Zhuan, recording that Duke Xiang of Song led the lords in an attack on Qi, says that the Qi people 'were unable to fight' — not that they had no men, but that no command existed to unite them. Song's method was to convert the covenant of assemblies directly into a military alliance: Duke Xiang took the troops of his own state as the core, the lords supplied chariots and foot in their several contingents, and the coalition moved north-west from Shangqiu, passed the line of Tao and Cao, then turned onto the routes north and south of Mount Tai and so came at last to the Qi capital of Linzi — some three hundred and fifty kilometres in all, which at the ordinary rate of thirty to fifty kilometres a day could be covered in about ten days; what mattered was not the speed but whether the coalition could keep its grain and its discipline. Having surrounded Linzi, Duke Xiang did not attempt to storm the walls, for the ramparts and the siege engines of the Spring and Autumn were not yet good enough to break a great city in a few days; he used the weight of his troops as the prop behind his terms, insisting that Qi must restore the departed crown prince Zhao according to the proper order of succession. Qi's response was to ask for terms first and then to settle matters from within, and at last it removed the most glaring of its opponents by itself: as the coalition pressed in, the clans of the state that had set themselves up at home fought it out within the walls, Prince Wufu was killed, the crown prince Zhao was welcomed back, and Qi bought off the withdrawal of the coalition with a compromise made inside its own gates. The whole process shows the logic of 'forcing a settlement by force' in the early Spring and Autumn: the coalition had no intention of annexing Qi, its object was to put a ruler of Qi on the throne whom the lords would acknowledge, and so the order of assemblies built by Duke Huan could be carried on. The lesson came at a heavy price for Song: it had bought the political credit of installing a ruler with the banner of the coalition, but had established no military prestige in a pitched battle, and a year later the battle of Hong ended in a crushing defeat for the Song army and a grave wound for Duke Xiang. Qi had a lesson of its own: once civil strife brings foreign chariots into the country, whichever faction wins pays for it by admitting foreign powers into the domestic politics of the state. There is no record of any large siege or set-piece battle in this conflict, yet it settled two rules for the early Spring and Autumn: first, the handover of hegemony could be accomplished through the covenant and through procedure at home, and did not necessarily require a slaughter beneath the walls; second, the clans of Qi had to find a new common ground, or the same kind of crisis would return.
data: 可引的數字大致如下。時間上，齊桓公於前685年即位、在位四十三年，前643年（魯隱公三年）冬去世，前642年（魯隱公四年）夏宋襄公以諸侯伐齊，齊威公在位約九年，前633年去世。疆域上，齊國在桓公末年東至渤海，西抵黃河西岸的河西之地，南與魯、鄭相接。城池上，考古測量所得臨淄齊故城大城周長約十五公里，小城（宮城）周長約三公里，是同時期東方最大的城邑之一，商賈、匠人與軍械都集中在小城之內。賦役上，齊國以「戈」為單位折算兵員，一繳若干戈即出若干甲士；《管子》一類後出的文獻保存了管仲理齊時「官山海」、通魚鹽之利的記述，這是齊國財政與軍費的根基。聯軍規模沒有確數：春秋諸侯會盟的常態是數千至一萬餘人，兵車數十至數百乘；《左傳》只作「諸侯之師」，不列人數。行程上，商丘至臨淄的直線距離約三百五十公里，聯軍若於夏初出發，十日上下可抵城下。戰果方面沒有可信的斬獲記載，齊國方面可確定的變化是公子無虧被殺、太子昭即位，其餘公子各有去留；宋國沒有取得土地，也沒有繳獲成建制的兵車。往後的關鍵數字是：前638年泓之戰宋襄公大敗於楚，前637年宋襄公去世，前632年城濮之戰晉文公破楚聯軍而取代齊國成為諸侯盟主，前489年前後齊國高氏、國氏覆亡，前386年田氏代齊、姜姓齊國終結，前481年齊國滅宋。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. On dates, Duke Huan of Qi took the throne in 685 BC and ruled for forty-three years; he died in the winter of 643 BC (the third year of Duke Yin of Lu); in the summer of 642 BC (the fourth year of Duke Yin) Duke Xiang of Song led the lords in an attack on Qi; and Duke Wei of Qi reigned for about nine years, dying in 633 BC. On territory, at the end of Duke Huan's reign Qi reached the Bohai sea in the east and the lands beyond the Yellow River in the west, and bordered Lu and Zheng in the south. On the city, the measured circuit of the great wall of the Qi capital at Linzi is about fifteen kilometres, and that of the smaller inner city about three kilometres, making it one of the largest urban centres in the east at the time, with merchants, craftsmen and the armourers all gathered inside the inner city. On levies, Qi reckoned its manning in ge, a levy of so many ge producing so many armoured men, and texts of the Mozi type that came down to us later preserve the account of how Guan Zhong administered Qi, with the mountains and the seas under state control and the profits of salt and fish opened up — the foundation of Qi's finances and of the money that paid for its army. There is no reliable figure for the size of the coalition: an assembly of lords in the Spring and Autumn commonly brought together several thousand men and occasionally more than ten thousand, with some tens to some hundreds of war chariots, and the Zuo Zhuan says only 'the army of the lords' without listing numbers. On distance, the direct line from Shangqiu to Linzi is about three hundred and fifty kilometres, so a coalition setting out in early summer could stand before the walls in about ten days. On results there is no trustworthy count of casualties, and the changes that can be firmly fixed on the Qi side are the killing of Prince Wufu and the enthronement of the crown prince Zhao, with the remaining princes going their several ways; Song took no land and captured no formed body of chariots. The key figures that follow are these: the Song army was routed by Chu at the battle of Hong in 638 BC; Duke Xiang of Song died in 637 BC; at the battle of Chengpu in 632 BC Duke Wen of Jin broke the Chu-led coalition and took over from Qi as hegemon of the lords; the Gao and Guo clans of Qi were extinguished about 489 BC; the Tian clan replaced the Jiang house of Qi in 386 BC, bringing the Jiang state to an end; and Qi annexed Song in 481 BC.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因可以分成四層。第一層是繼承制度本身：齊國的君位由姜姓呂氏一系掌握，諸公子各有封邑與武裝，國君一死，誰來繼承本應由名分與實力共同決定，而兩者此時並不一致，桓公在位四十三年所建立的權威也隨之崩解。第二層是桓公晚年的失政：前645年管仲病故，齊國失去整頓朝政、壓制公族的核心人物，易牙、豎貂與公子開方以寵幸之身參預國政，長子太子昭的儲位被削，桓公臨終之際既未確定嗣君，也未把兵權交給可託孤的大臣，國史記載他死後屍身久停方得入殮，宮禁之權全落在內豎與諸公子之間。第三層是諸侯會盟體系本身的壓力：齊桓公以「九合諸侯」把齊國推到盟主位置，會盟所維持的是一種各國都承認的秩序，霸主的更替必須有諸侯見證；一旦齊國的君位由國內少數派系私定，秩序的表面完整就會破裂，這正是宋國得以號召聯軍的正當理由。第四層是宋國自身的戰略動機：宋襄公即位以來一直以接替桓公、延續霸業自居，他既需要在諸侯面前證明宋國有能力召集大軍，也需要一場名義正當、可以見功於會盟的行動；把出奔的太子昭送回齊國，既解除了齊國的合法疑慮，又讓宋國成了新君的恩主。地理與經濟層面同樣不可忽視：齊國地處海岱之間，四面與魯、鄭、衛、燕相接，臨淄一城而天下注視；宋國正當其西，一旦齊國內部失序，宋國是最直接受益於收拾局面、並在隨後數年裡爭取霸權的國家。於是四層因素交疊，戰爭在桓公逝世的當年就成為可能。
causeEn: The origins of this war fall into four layers. The first is the succession system itself: the throne of Qi was held by the Jiang surname and the Lü clan, the several princes had their own fiefs and their own armed followers, and once the ruler died the question of who should succeed ought to have been settled by rank and by strength together — except that the two no longer agreed, and the authority that Duke Huan had built over forty-three years collapsed with him. The second is the failure of his last years: Guan Zhong fell ill and died in 645 BC, and Qi lost the one man capable of disciplining the court and holding the great clans in check; Yi Ya, Shu Diao and Prince Kaifang took part in government as favourites, the position of the eldest son, the crown prince Zhao, was cut away, and at the end of his life Duke Huan neither named an heir nor left the armed force in the hands of a minister he could trust; the histories record that his body lay long before it could be coffined, and the authority of the inner court fell entirely to the eunuchs and the princes. The third is the pressure of the covenant of assemblies itself: by his nine meetings of the lords Duke Huan had carried Qi to the place of hegemon, and what the assemblies maintained was an order that every state acknowledged, so that the handover of the overlordship had to be witnessed by the lords; once the throne of Qi was settled privately by a few factions at home, the outward completeness of that order would break, and this is precisely the sound reason by which Song could call a coalition into the field. The fourth is Song's own strategic motive: Duke Xiang of Song had set himself up as the continuator of Duke Huan and the carrier of the hegemony ever since his accession, and he needed both to show the lords that Song could muster a great army and to have an action that was righteous in form and would be talked about in the assemblies; restoring the departed crown prince Zhao to Qi removed the legitimate doubt hanging over Qi and at the same time made Song the benefactor of the new ruler. Geography and economics matter no less: Qi lay between the sea and Mount Tai, touching Lu, Zheng, Wei and Yan on every side, and the single city of Linzi was watched by all; Song lay directly to its west, and once the order inside Qi broke down, Song was the state most likely to profit from picking up the pieces and from pressing its claim to the hegemony in the years that followed. The four layers thus overlapped, and a war became possible in the very year of Duke Huan's death.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是齊國的君位以一種對外國負責的方式解決：太子昭回國即位為齊威公，齊國避免了諸公子分立國家與長期內戰的結局。但代價同樣清楚。齊國的霸權就此轉移：前638年宋襄公在泓之戰中大敗於楚，前637年而死，宋國反而陷入連續內亂；前632年城濮之戰，晉文公破楚聯軍並成為諸侯盟主，齊國此後退守東方兩百餘年，直到前481年滅宋才重回中原霸主的角色。其次，這場干預確立了春秋時期諸侯介入他國內政的先例：盟主的君位不再只是本國的家族事務，而成了會盟體系裡各國共同監督的對象，齊國此後每一次的君位更替——從齊孝公到齊莊公、齊襄公，再到崔、慶、陳三族當權——都發生在諸侯的注視之下。再次，齊國宗族政治的根由也在這場危機中顯形：國氏、高氏與陳氏在桓公死後各自押注，最終陳氏一系逐步坐大，前489年前後高氏、國氏相覆亡，前386年田和廢齊康公，姜姓齊國易為田氏齊國，齊國從此由田氏執政，這一變化比任何一次會盟都更深地改變了東方的政治格局。最後是技術與制度的層面：齊國的戈兵制式、兵車戰與賦役徵發在戰亂中受損又重建，管仲「官山海」的理齊之政在此後數代仍被追憶，而楚、秦的鐵器在此後兩百年間逐步推進，春秋早期以青銅戈矛為主的戰場裝備並沒有長久維持下去；至於卡面那件亞述長矛，它提醒人們同時代的亞述帝國仍在用短柄長刃的鐵矛維持著西亞與北非的秩序，而東方的齊國正靠青銅戈矛與兵車守住自己的疆界——兩套截然不同的武器體系，隔著萬里之遙同時存在於這個時代。
impactEn: The direct result of the war was that the throne of Qi was settled in a manner answerable to a foreign power: the crown prince Zhao came home and was enthroned as Duke Wei, and Qi was spared the spectacle of the several princes each becoming a separate state and of a long civil war. The cost was just as clear. Qi's hegemony moved away: Duke Xiang of Song was crushed by Chu at the battle of Hong in 638 BC and died in 637 BC, and Song itself fell into a run of internal disorders; at Chengpu in 632 BC Duke Wen of Jin broke the Chu coalition and became hegemon of the lords, and Qi then held to the east for more than two hundred years, only returning to the role of hegemon in the central plain when it annexed Song in 481 BC. Second, the intervention set a precedent for the lords meddling in each other's domestic affairs: the succession of an overlord was no longer a private family matter of one state but something the whole assembly watched, and every subsequent change of ruler in Qi — from Duke Xiao and Duke Zhuang to Duke Xiang, and on to the years when the Cui, the Qing and the Chen clans held power — took place under the gaze of the other lords. Third, the roots of Qi's clan politics were laid bare by this crisis: the Guo, the Gao and the Chen clans each placed their bets after Duke Huan's death, and in the end the Chen line grew to dominate; the Gao and Guo clans were extinguished about 489 BC, and in 386 BC Tian He deposed Duke Kang, so that the Jiang house of Qi gave way to the Tian house of Qi, and Qi was thereafter ruled by the Tian clan — a change that altered the political map of the east far more deeply than any assembly of lords. Last is the level of technique and institutions: Qi's standard ge-armed infantry, its chariot warfare and its levy system were damaged by the war and then rebuilt, Guan Zhong's government of Qi with the mountains and the seas under state control was still remembered for generations afterwards, and the iron of Chu and Qin advanced over the following two centuries, so that the battlefield equipment of the early Spring and Autumn, bronze ge and mao, did not long endure. As for the Assyrian spear on the card, it is a reminder that the Assyrian empire of the same age was still maintaining its order in western Asia and North Africa with short-shafted, long-bladed iron spears, while Qi in the east held its own frontier with bronze ge and mao and with war chariots: two entirely different weapon systems, separated by ten thousand li, existing at the same moment in this age.
result: 就軍事過程而言，這是一場以極少流血換取政治目的的戰爭。齊國沒有能力抵抗——國中分黨，禁軍與公族武裝互不統一，齊人在《左傳》的記載裡是「弗能戰」；宋國則沒有攻城器械，也沒有在會盟諸侯面前強攻大國城郭的打算。聯軍推進到臨淄城下，齊國先請和，繼而在城內清除公子無虧，迎太子昭回國，齊威公即位，宋襄公與諸侯之師退去。從齊國的立場看，這是一場以讓出部分內政自主權換取王位穩固的敗局；從宋國的立場看，這是一場名成功而實失敗的勝利：宋國完成了送還合法君主的政治目標，卻沒有取得任何土地，沒有一輛繳獲的兵車，也沒有一場可以證明軍力的會戰。一年之後，泓之戰的結果讓宋國的虛實暴露於諸侯面前，宋襄公傷重而卒，宋國隨之陷入長久的內亂，霸權的路線就此轉到楚成王、再轉到晉文公之手。齊威公在位約九年，前633年卒；其後齊國的君位在孝公與莊公之間幾度更替，內部公族之爭並未因此收束，反而在往後數十年裡愈演愈烈，直至田氏代齊、齊國的性質徹底改變。回頭看，這場前643年至前642年的繼承人戰爭，是春秋秩序一次典型的低成本運作：用聯軍的兵威解決了一個大國的家事，維持住了諸侯會盟的表面，卻把齊國的內部裂痕與宋國的虛弱同時暴露在光下。真正的解決要再等一百餘年——前481年齊滅宋、前386年田氏代齊，才算把東方的這盤棋收到另一種局面裡。
resultEn: In its military process this was a war that bought a political purpose at very little cost in blood. Qi had no capacity to resist — the state was split into factions, the palace guard and the armed bands of the great clans were not united, and the Qi people in the account of the Zuo Zhuan 'were unable to fight'. Song had no siege engines either, nor any intention of assaulting the walls of a great state in front of the assembled lords. The coalition pressed forward to the walls of Linzi, Qi asked for terms first and then removed Prince Wufu from within its own gates, welcomed the crown prince Zhao home, and Duke Wei of Qi took the throne while Duke Xiang and the army of the lords withdrew. From Qi's point of view this was a defeat purchased by surrendering part of its freedom in domestic affairs in exchange for a settled throne; from Song's point of view it was a nominal success and a real failure: Song achieved its political object of restoring a rightful ruler, but took no land, captured not a single chariot, and fought no pitched battle that could demonstrate its strength. A year later the battle of Hong laid bare the weakness of Song before the other lords; Duke Xiang of Song died of his wounds, Song fell into a long period of internal disorder, and the road of the hegemony passed to King Cheng of Chu and then to Duke Wen of Jin. Duke Wei of Qi reigned for about nine years and died in 633 BC; after him the throne of Qi changed hands several times between Duke Xiao and Duke Zhuang, and the quarrels of the great clans were not thereby settled, but grew worse over the decades that followed, until the Tian clan replaced the Jiang house and the very nature of Qi was altered. Looked at from a distance, this war of 643 to 642 BC was a typical low-cost working of the Spring and Autumn order: the weight of a coalition's troops settled the domestic affairs of a great state, kept up the outward appearance of the assemblies of lords, and at the same time exposed both the fissures inside Qi and the weakness of Song to the light. The real settlement had to wait a further century and more: the annexation of Song by Qi in 481 BC and the replacement of the Jiang house by the Tian house in 386 BC were what finally turned the eastern board into a different kind of position.
